parsed.notes: Lens B only. I did not search outside the disclosed files and did not raise support or quote-fidelity findings except where a disclosed later limitation affected the live-law framing.

reasons: Texas v. Cobb is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 532 U.S. 162.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note confirms Cobb defines Sixth Amendment scope by the Blockburger same-elements test.
Rothgery v. Gillespie County is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority and the citation 554 U.S. 191 appears in citations.all.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
No disclosed treatment edge supersedes or overrules the attachment proposition.
residual_risks: The treatment scope note is generic rather than proposition-specific, but it still records good_law and no point overrides.

reasons: United States v. Ash is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 413 U.S. 300.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note states Ash remains good law for no Sixth Amendment right to counsel at a photographic display.
Simmons v. United States is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 390 U.S. 377.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note says the photographic-identification due-process standard remains good law.
United States v. Wade is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 388 U.S. 218.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note records later limits by Kirby and Ash, but the assertion is framed as a post-indictment lineup and does not conflict with those limits.
United States v. Crews is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 445 U.S. 463.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note states the independent-source analysis of an in-court identification remains good law.
Kirby v. Illinois is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 406 U.S. 682.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note confirms the plurality attachment rule was later adopted by a majority and reaffirmed in Rothgery.
Gilbert v. California is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 388 U.S. 263.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note recognizes the Kirby limitation, and the assertion is framed as a post-charge lineup.
residual_risks: Lens B does not resolve whether the phrase 'no harmless-error' is support-precise; no disclosed treatment field invalidates the Gilbert rule.

reasons: Neil v. Biggers is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 409 U.S. 188.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note says the five reliability factors were carried forward in Manson and remain good law.
Perry v. New Hampshire is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority and the citation 565 U.S. 228 appears in citations.all.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
No disclosed treatment edge supersedes or overrules Perry's police-arrangement threshold.
residual_risks: The treatment scope note is generic rather than proposition-specific, but it still records good_law and no point overrides.

reasons: Stovall v. Denno is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 388 U.S. 293.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note says the due-process suggestiveness holding remains good law, with the reliability framework later developed by Biggers and Manson.
Manson v. Brathwaite is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 432 U.S. 98.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note says Perry confirmed the police-arrangement threshold without disturbing Manson's reliability factors.
Foster v. California is identified as U.S. Supreme Court authority with citation 394 U.S. 440.
Lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
The scope note describes Foster as good law and as the rare case finding a pretrial identification so suggestive as to violate due process.

defect.evidence_quote: The *[[United States v. Wade\|Wade]]* counsel-at-lineup right is **offense-specific**: counsel is required only for a lineup concerning the **charged** offense; a post-charge lineup on a different, uncharged offense triggers no *Wade/Gilbert* right.
defect.locator_note: Black-letter callout ^rule-eyewitness; limitation is disclosed in the Texas v. Cobb inventory row and lake treatment marks Cobb good_law.
defect.problem: The black-letter Sixth Amendment sentence says a post-attachment corporeal lineup is a critical stage with counsel, but it omits the disclosed offense-specific limitation supplied by Cobb. As framed, it can overstate the live Wade/Gilbert rule for a lineup about a different, uncharged offense.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: 'a post-attachment corporeal lineup concerning the charged offense, or the same offense under Cobb/Blockburger, is a critical stage...'

reasons: Wade, Manson, and Perry are each marked good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
Texas v. Cobb is also marked good_law and the disclosed Cobb row expressly limits the Wade lineup right to the charged offense.
This is a currency/treatment limitation, not a support or quote-fidelity challenge.
residual_risks: Support and quote fidelity of the cited cases were not assessed under lens B.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the Cobb offense-specific qualifier directly in the black-letter rule.
